title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: Within Gd(III) clusters of comparable design, stronger intracluster antiferromagnetic coupling lowers −ΔSM relative to the value expected from spin density, whereas very weak coupling lets −ΔSM approach the calculated full spin entropy.
explanation: The authors describe −ΔSM as linear with magnetic spin density, with points above the line for weaker interactions and below it for stronger ones. Gd24 reaches 46.1 J kg−1 K−1 versus a theoretical 52.1 J kg−1 K−1 and has a Weiss temperature of about −0.16 K. Gd36, despite high spin density, has a smaller −ΔSM of 39.6 J kg−1 K−1 and a more negative Weiss temperature (−2.41 K).
scope: High-nuclearity Gd(III) hydroxide clusters whose MCE is compared with spin density and bulk susceptibility (Weiss θ).
conditions: Isothermal entropy change compared with nR ln(2S+1)-type theoretical limits and with the sign and magnitude of antiferromagnetic coupling.
caveats: Weiss temperatures are bulk indicators, not a full exchange Hamiltonian. One later sentence in the Markdown also quotes −ΔSM = 41.8 J kg−1 K−1 and θ = −3.57 for Gd48, which conflicts with an earlier numerical assignment and should be verified.
